WMT.rationale: Walmart is a wide-moat franchise with durable competitive advantages (31% online grocery share, 15 consecutive quarters of 10%+ e-commerce growth, 46% advertising growth to $6.4B). Revenue grew +7.3% YoY and EPS +19.6% YoY in Q1 FY2026, with stable gross margins (~25.1%) and improving ROE (21.6% to 23%). However, the near-term picture is mixed: operating cash flow declined -12.4% YoY and -47.9% QoQ despite rising net income, creating an earnings-quality concern. Quarterly EPS is non-monotonic ($0.56→$0.88→$0.77→$0.67), with Q1 FY2026 the weakest of the last three quarters. Valuation has compressed to 38.7x PE (floor of 365-day range 37.6-55.4x), which is cheap vs own history but still demanding in absolute terms given a 2.6% earnings yield vs 4.49% 10Y Treasury. The Cleveland Research note flagging slowing U.S. comps and the ~20% decline from May highs reflect repricing of near-term execution risk. The oil collapse (-39%) is a genuine margin tailwind. Net: strong franchise, fair-to-slightly-cheap vs own history, but deteriorating cash conversion and still-elevated absolute multiple cap the score. A modest positive tilt reflects the structural quality and valuation floor, with the August earnings report as a potential re-rating event if cash flow normalizes.
